sections.Profile:
"Viking" is a two-player electro-mechanical pinball machine released by Williams Electronic Manufacturing Company in June 1960. Designed by Harry Mabs, the game features two flippers, four pop bumpers, two passive bumpers, two slingshots, four standup targets, two kick-out holes, and a gobble hole. The machine showcases a distinctive cabinet design known as the "Styling of the 60's," which includes anodized aluminum trim, tapered tubular chromium steel legs, and a built-in shelf with a cigarette holder, allowing players to place drinks while playing.
